speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You present with progressive difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and speech difficulties. To begin my assessment, please tell me: for how long have these symptoms been occurring, and did they start suddenly or gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

The clinical picture of progressive quadriparesis, urinary incontinence, and bulbar symptoms (slurred speech) in a 54-year-old male is highly concerning for ALS. While incontinence is atypical for pure motor neuron disease, the rapid progression and combination of motor and bulbar signs strongly suggest a diagnosis that requires immediate confirmation with MRI of the brain and spine, as well as EMG/NCS.
